title: Static Testing Objectives
concept:
Static testing has multiple objectives that overlap with — but are distinct from — those of dynamic testing.

**Defect detection in work products** — finding ambiguities, contradictions, missing pieces, errors. Because static testing examines the artifact directly, it finds the defect at its source rather than via downstream symptoms.

**Improving the quality of the work product** — reviews and static analysis catch quality issues (clarity, maintainability, conformance) that dynamic testing cannot.

**Conformance to standards** — reviews and static analysis check whether the work product follows applicable standards (coding standards, regulatory standards, organisational templates).

**Building consensus** — reviews bring stakeholders together around the work product and surface disagreements early.

**Knowledge transfer** — review participants learn the content of the work product and gain shared understanding.

**Risk identification** — reviewers may flag risks (unclear assumptions, missing edge cases, performance concerns) that drive subsequent test planning.

A test plan should state which objectives apply for each review; tracking review effectiveness against these objectives is part of test process improvement.
keyPoints: Static testing objectives: detect defects, improve quality, check standards conformance, build consensus, transfer knowledge, identify risks.
Different reviews target different objectives — a code inspection emphasises defect detection; a sprint demo emphasises consensus.
Tracking which objectives each review meets helps tune the review process.

quiz.question: Which static testing objective is BEST served by a structured peer review of newly-written acceptance criteria with the product owner, developer, and tester present?
options: Building consensus among stakeholders that the criteria are clear and complete.
quiz.explanation: Reviewing acceptance criteria with multiple stakeholders is the classic 'three amigos' meeting whose primary objective is building consensus on what 'done' means. Memory leaks and stress testing are dynamic activities; code coverage is measured during dynamic execution.
